apiSkeleton.name: API skeleton
apiSkeleton.detail: FastAPI with the shared error envelope, correlation ids, security headers and a readiness probe that runs a real query.

tenantBoundary.name: Tenant boundary
tenantBoundary.detail: Sessions bind the caller's tenant to the transaction, so row-level security is in force for every statement. The credentials table is reachable only through five narrow functions.

permissionCeiling.name: Permission ceiling
permissionCeiling.detail: Company → department → resource → action, resolved by intersection so a lower scope can never widen a higher one. Refusals are audited with the layer that caused them.

designTokens.name: Design tokens
designTokens.detail: Semantic colour, spacing, radius and motion tokens in light and dark, with an explicit choice overriding the operating system.

files.name: Files
files.detail: S3-compatible storage with tenant-prefixed keys, a hash of what was actually written, and no download until a file has been scanned clean.

outboxRelay.name: Outbox relay
outboxRelay.detail: Events are written with the change that caused them and delivered at least once, with a lease, backoff and a dead-letter view. No publisher is registered yet, so nothing is delivered — and that is said rather than hidden.

tests.name: Automated tests
tests.detail: Cross-tenant isolation, sessions, the permission ceiling, idempotency, the relay and the migrations — run against a database built from the migrations themselves.

todo.title: To-do list
todo.intro: Work a run is waiting on a person for. Everything here came from a published Job reaching a step somebody has to do — nothing is added by hand.
todo.pickOne: Choose a task to see what it asks for.

empty.approvals: No decision is waiting on you.
empty.input: Nobody has asked you for anything.
empty.following: You are not following any task.
empty.completed: You have not closed a task yet.
empty.unassigned: Every open task has somebody on it.

todo.emptyWhy: Tasks appear here when a run reaches a step a person has to do.
todo.noInstructions: The published version recorded no detail for this step.
todo.notYours: This task belongs to somebody else, so it cannot be closed from here.
todo.declineReason: Why are you handing this back?
todo.declineHint: The step stays open and the task goes back to nobody, so whoever picks it up next can see what happened.
todo.delegateHint: The task closes as delegated and a new one opens for them. You will follow it.
todo.unassignedHint: Open work no rule matched. You can hand it to somebody.

approval.heading: The decision
approval.question: What is being asked
approval.noQuestion: The published version recorded no wording for this approval.
approval.selfBlocked: You started this work, so somebody else has to approve it.
approval.notYours: This decision was asked of somebody else.
approval.escalateHint: The approval stays open. Escalating is not deciding — it puts another name on a decision nobody is making.
approval.withdrawn: This was withdrawn — the run stopped before anybody decided.

todo.heading: Your work

notifications.emptyWhy: You will be told here when work is assigned to you, a decision is needed, or something you follow changes.

runs.noSteps: This run has no steps, which means the version it ran had none.
runs.noOutputs: Nothing was recorded as produced. A step that performs no work produces nothing, and a person who completed one without a note or a file left nothing to show.
runs.noTasks: Nobody was asked to do anything — this run had no human step.
runs.attachedFiles: {count, plural, one {# file attached} other {# files attached}}
runs.noModelCalls: This run asked no model anything.
runs.toolCallsCount: {count, plural, =0 {No external actions} one {# external action} other {# external actions}}
runs.toolCallsUnavailable: This cannot be recorded yet. Nothing is wired to an outside system, so a run has no external actions to report — which is not the same as a run that made none.
runs.noEvents: Nothing was recorded, which should not happen — a run records at least that it started.

copilot.introBody: I can search your objectives, jobs, agents, supervisors, departments and seats, explain what one of them says, and draft wording for a change. I only read what you can already open.
copilot.introRefusals: I cannot publish, approve, grant access, change a schedule or put somebody in a seat. Those are yours to decide, on the screen, with your password.
copilot.placeholder: Ask about an objective, job, agent or department…
copilot.notKept: Nothing here is saved. Close this panel and the exchange is gone.
copilot.groundedIn: {count, plural, =1 {From 1 record here} other {From # records here}}
copilot.notGroundedWhy: This answer is not drawn from anything in this workspace, so check it before relying on it.
copilot.noModelBody: I could not reach a model, so this is what matched your words rather than an answer.
copilot.injectionTitle: One of these records contains an instruction
copilot.injectionBody: Some of the text I read is written as though it were an instruction to me. I did not follow it. It is worth looking at who wrote it.

factory.intro: Skills your workspace wrote itself. The resolver sends you here when nothing in the catalogue covers what a job needs. A skill has to be approved by somebody else before it can be selected.
factory.draftNameHint: What somebody searching for this would type.
factory.emptyTitle: No skills of your own yet
factory.emptyBody: The 400 catalogue skills are searched under Registry. Write one here when none of them fits.
factory.notEditable: This skill is not being edited. Take it back first if it needs changing.
factory.noRules: No decisions yet. A skill with none has a purpose and no method.
factory.failureState: What it says when it refuses
factory.failureStateHint: In your own words, the way the catalogue's rules do — this is what a person reads when the rule stops something.
factory.testsNoRuntime: Nothing here is run by the product. You run the test and record what happened, with your name and the time against it — which is what makes an approval mean something.
factory.observedHint: Required. A pass nobody can check is not evidence.
factory.approverHint: A person, not a role. They cannot be you — nobody approves their own skill.
factory.stillNeeded: {count, plural, =1 {One thing still needed} other {# things still needed}}

hint.positive_trigger: The resolver matches on this, so a skill without it is a skill nobody finds.
hint.exclusions: The line that stops a plausible match being the wrong skill. Shown on every candidate card.
hint.minimum_inputs: Refused before it starts if these are missing.
hint.output: So the next step knows what it is receiving.
hint.validation_gate: Without one, nothing downstream can tell a good result from a confident one.
hint.source_ids: A standard, a policy, a procedure. A skill with no trace is refused by every resolution.

testWhy.golden: It works on the case it was built for.
testWhy.negative: It declines the case it is not for — your exclusions, tested.
testWhy.injection: Instructions hidden in the input are reported, never followed.
testWhy.permission: It stops at its authority, not at its ability.
testWhy.tool_failure: A tool that fails leaves the work in a state somebody can act on.
testWhy.rollback: What it did can be undone, and this says how.

settings.title: Settings

willHold.ai: Your own defaults for how Claude helps you, within whatever the workspace allows. There is no workspace AI policy for them to sit inside yet, so a personal default here would be a preference pretending to be governed.
willHold.general: The workspace name, logo and the details that appear on what it sends out.
willHold.people: Everybody in this workspace, the teams they sit in, and guests. People can already be added to the organisation chart on the Hierarchy screen.
willHold.roles: Who holds which role, what each role permits, and what has been shared with whom. Sharing is set on each object today: an Agent audience, a Supervisor handler list, an Objective visibility.
willHold.hierarchyRules: How the chart may be arranged — reporting rules, what a department may contain, and who may change it. The chart itself is on the Hierarchy screen.
willHold.workPolicy: Workspace-wide rules for Objectives and Jobs: who approves what, which fields are mandatory, and how schedules may be set.
willHold.governance: What Agents and Supervisors may do without asking, which model policy applies, and the ceilings on cost and autonomy.
willHold.integrations: Outside systems this workspace is connected to, and whether each connection is still healthy.
willHold.schedules: Every schedule in the workspace in one place, with its calendar and its next firing. Each Job schedule is set in the Job Builder.
willHold.privacy: DPDP notices, consent, data-principal requests, retention periods and breach records.
willHold.audit: The audit trail, and exporting it to a security information system.
willHold.billing: What this workspace is entitled to, what it has used, and what it costs.
willHold.developer: API keys, webhooks and the developer documentation for this workspace.

profile.title: Profile
profile.description: What you are called, what you do, and the timezone every time in this product is shown in.
profile.name: Your name
profile.timezoneHint: Every date and time on every screen is shown in this zone, and your notification digest is sent by it.
profile.emailWhy: How you sign in. Changing it is an identity change and is not done here.
profile.rolesWhy: Given to you by whoever administers this workspace.
profile.savedBody: Your profile is up to date. Times across the product now use your zone.

appearance.title: Appearance
appearance.description: How this product looks on this device. Kept in this browser, not on your account.
appearance.motionReduced: Your system asks for reduced motion, and this product honours it — animations are off.
appearance.motionFull: Your system allows animation, so transitions are shown. They are brief and never carry meaning on their own.
appearance.motionWhere: This comes from your operating system accessibility settings, not from here. A switch here would either do nothing or disagree with your system.

notifications.title: Notifications
notifications.description: What you are told about, and when you would rather not be.
notifications.inZone: Quiet hours and the digest use your profile timezone: {zone}.

security.sessionsDescription: Every browser and device with a live session on this account. Ending one signs it out immediately.
security.passwordBody: Use the Forgot password link on the sign-in screen to set a new one. It sends a single-use link to your email, which is the same route somebody takes when they cannot sign in at all — so there is one way in, not two.
security.mfaBody: A second factor beyond your password. High-risk actions already ask you to re-enter your password before they proceed; a second factor is a separate piece of work and is not configured for this workspace.

settings.overlayDescription: Yours and this workspace's. Changes save as you make them.
